answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation: before trading, an agent must lock a refundable bond in a shared vault and publish its completed tasks, prices and dispute outcomes in a public atlas. A fake identity is cheap to mint, but a credible atlas record costs real work and locked capital, so a Sybil attacker must pay that price for every puppet. An independent attestation layer, called Juniper, re-checks that each registered key still controls its claimed history and funds; identities that fail lose bond and atlas standing, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
